ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, \( R_1 = 50k\Omega \), \( R_2 = 25k\Omega \). For the circuit to realize the analog addition operation \( u_0 = -(2u_{i1} + 4u_{i2}) \), \( R_f = \) ________ kΩ.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two input signals u_i1 and u_i2, respectively connected through resistors R1 and R2 to the same summing node; this node is connected to the inverting input terminal of the operational amplifier, and the output terminal is connected back to this node through the feedback resistor Rf. The non-inverting input terminal of the operational amplifier is grounded through R3. Therefore this circuit is an inverting adder. Reasoning: The output of the inverting summing amplifier is u0 = -(Rf/R1)u_i1 - (Rf/R2)u_i2. The problem requires u0 = -(2u_i1 + 4u_i2), so Rf/R1 = 2 and Rf/R2 = 4 are needed. Substituting R1 = 50 kΩ gives Rf = 2 × 50 = 100 kΩ; substituting R2 = 25 kΩ gives Rf = 4 × 25 = 100 kΩ, and the two are consistent.
